title: Stream request-cache serialization to reduce peak memory
body:
## Problem

Request-cache writes first materialize the entire pickle with `dill.dumps`, and reads first retain the complete file with `file.read()`. Large cached request collections therefore need an additional serialized-data-sized allocation alongside their actual objects.

## Change

Use dill's file interfaces (`dump` and `load`) to serialize and deserialize through the already-open binary file. Cache keys, file names, protocol defaults, directory creation, disabled-cache behavior, and exception-to-cache-miss handling stay the same. Existing cache files remain readable, and new cache bytes match the previous serializer.

## Validation

- Original implementation: **2 memory-regression failures, 10 semantic tests passed**.
- Patched implementation: **18 passed**, covering all 12 new tests and the complete existing `tests/test_cache.py` module.
- Existing dill protocols 3, 4, and 5, exact serialized bytes, `Instance` metadata and shared references, recursive/callable payloads, corrupt/missing/disabled caches are covered.
- A real `ConfigurableTask` builds requests, writes the cache, restores a limited request set in a fresh task, and processes a result successfully.
- Ruff 0.16.3 checks, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.

### Local memory and timing

Measured on a shared CPU environment using one warmup and seven timed calls per case. Peak Python allocation was measured separately with `tracemalloc`. Every original/patched cache file has the same SHA-256, and every restored object equals its input.

| Payload | Original write peak | Patched write peak | Original read peak | Patched read peak |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 100 requests, roughly 1 KiB context each | 309,993 B | 201,400 B | 383,939 B | 272,020 B |
| 1,000 requests, roughly 8 KiB context each | 10,548,001 B | 1,446,916 B | 17,795,904 B | 9,507,308 B |
| Single 8 MiB byte payload | 9,445,476 B | 8,093 B | 16,784,941 B | 8,404,107 B |

For the 1,000-request fixture, median write time was 26.279 → 25.504 ms and read time was 2.312 → 2.021 ms. For the small 100-request fixture, write time was 2.322 → 2.366 ms and read time was 0.116 → 0.115 ms. The benefit is reduced serialization memory; small-cache latency is effectively unchanged in this measurement and is not claimed to improve universally.

These measurements cover cache I/O and serialization only. The full harness suite and model inference were not run. Request objects and dill's memo still occupy memory proportional to the cached data; the cache is not made lazy, and this change does not add atomic writes or change cache-key semantics.

## Related work

Checked all-state request-cache/serialization/dill/stream searches, all six actual source-history patches, personal PR history, and the actual pre-existing fork commits. The current 144 fork heads differ from the prior audit only by the already-published SCORE counting change. Existing file-name work (#4446 and #4547) and response-cache coalescing (#4588) address different paths and are not included here.
